Dan "apEX" Madesclaire (born February 22, 1993) is a French professional Counter-Strike 2 player who plays for Team Vitality as the in-game leader and an entry fragger and a former Counter-Strike: Global Offensive and Counter-Strike: Source player. An entry fragger in the earlier days of Global Offensive, known for his aggression; he transitioned to the IGL role in March 2020 after ALEX's departure from Team Vitality.

apEX is among the most decorated players in Global Offensive and Counter-Strike 2 history, having won over 35 S-Tier tournaments across his career. Among these accomplishments include four Majors and two ESL Grand Slam trophies.

Trivia

[edit]

Personal

[edit]
  • He is one of the only players to have changed teams with every "French Shuffle", moving to Titan in the first, Team EnVyUs in the second, G2 Esports in the third and finally Team Vitality in the fourth.

Awards

[edit]
  • Was voted the French breakout Counter-Strike: Source player of 2010 by VaKarM. [4]
  • Was ranked the 15th best player of 2014 by HLTV. [5]
  • Was ranked the 18th best player of 2015 by HLTV. [6]
  • Awarded IGL of the Year 2023 by HLTV. [7]
  • Awarded IGL of the Year 2025 by HLTV. [8]

Records

[edit]
  • Most Majors played (22).
    • Tied with karrigan
  • Previously held the record for oldest Major winner at 32 years and 121 days old. He dethroned karrigan as the former oldest major winner, who won PGL Major Antwerp 2022 at 32 years and 42 days old, until he was overtaken by karrigan, who won IEM Cologne Major 2026 at 36 years and 68 days old.
  • Oldest ESL Grand Slam winner, winning Season VI at 33 years and 56 days old. He dethroned karrigan as the former oldest ESL Grand Slam winner, who won Intel Grand Slam 4 at 32 years and 346 days old.
  • Second player in history to make three Major finals with three different cores.
  • Only player in history to win three Major finals with three different cores.
